text:
alex: 🚨 Customer P0 — multiple 502/504s hitting /v1/generate for large-batch jobs (batch_size >= 64). Customer reports timeouts and failed invoices. Opening triage here.
priya: oncall ack. which region and model? any pattern on payload size?
alex: eu-west-1, using redwood/xl-quant2. Errors spike for requests >64 inputs or tokens >2048. CPU on gateway looks normal, but gateway logs show connection resets.
matt: digging into LB and proxy logs now. seeing 504s from runtime-proxy to runtime-pool on a subset of pods. attaching snip: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] proxy -> runtime-pool: POST /infer 504 upstream read timeout
[upstream_conn] idle timeout exceeded
```
sasha: noted. could be queue depth exhaustion on the pool. are we hitting the batching/capacity limits?
alex: customer load pattern: spikes of large concurrent batched requests every ~30s. They use our /batch endpoint with parallel clients.
priya: can we temporarily throttle batch_size at the gateway for that customer to prevent pool stalls?
jamie: yes, we can push a per-customer config to cap batch_size=32 and max_concurrency=4. want me to rollout now?
alex: please do a config patch and route that customer's api-key to the new policy. Also enable verbose runtime logs for the pool serving that customer.
ops-bot: deploy-started: routing-rule patch to api-key XXXXXX -> applied to gateway-canary (2/6).
matt: after canary, we're still seeing a few 504s but lower. Looks like some runtime pods are dropping TLS keepalives under high KV cache pressure.
sasha: KV cache pressure — interesting. are large batches causing longer decoding times and expanding KV usage leading to slower response for concurrent requests?
priya: assigning immediate mitigations: (1) throttle customer batch_size (jamie) (2) scale runtime-pool by +30% (matt) (3) enable prefix cache eviction on those pods (sasha).
jamie: throttling in canary applied; customer reports error rate dropped by ~70% in last 5m. rolling to 6/6 now.
matt: scale up triggered, added 6 pods to pool; health checks green. still collecting traces.
sasha: enabling aggressive KV prefix eviction on the scaled pods. hoping to reduce per-request memory pressure.
alex: customer comms: notifying them of temporary throttling and targeted scaling. they requested root cause and ETA for full fix.
priya: who owns postmortem + permanent fix? I propose: (A) improve guidance and enforce soft batch_size limits per model (product) - jamie; (B) runtime: make KV eviction more robust and add backpressure metrics - sasha; (C) gateway: add per-key adaptive throttling policy and better circuit indicators - matt; (D) billing review for failed requests - finance contact jamie to handle credits.
jamie: ack for product and billing. will draft customer email and credits proposal.
sasha: will own runtime instrumentation and a follow-up bug to ensure keepalive stability under high KV churn.
matt: will add a synthetic load test that mimics concurrent large batches, add alerting when runtime upstream latency p50 > 500ms for >1m.
priya: next steps (short): 1) confirm throttling fully rolled (jamie) 2) confirm pool scale and eviction applied (matt/sasha) 3) capture traces and store in incident bucket (alex) 4) send initial customer update in 30min with mitigation details (jamie).
alex: timeline: initial mitigation reduced errors. still tracking root cause. keeping channel open. please add action items to deck.
--- 24h follow-up ---
alex: quick postmortem update: initial cause = runtime pool queue saturation + KV cache pressure from very large batches causing stuck coroutines and keepalive expiries. Throttling + scale reduced immediate customer impact.
jamie: customer accepted temporary throttling and requested timeline for permanent fix. Sent draft credit note for failed requests in last 48h.
sasha: action items created: 1) KV eviction tuning + telemetry (PR #4521) owner: sasha, ETA: 2026-03-22 2) coroutine watchdog to kill stuck decoders (PR #4523) owner: sasha, ETA: 2026-03-20.
matt: infra action: 3) gateway adaptive throttling by api-key (RFC + rollout) owner: matt, ETA: 2026-04-01. 4) synthetic test and alerting (issue #2304) owner: matt, ETA: 2026-03-18.
jamie: product/billing: 5) soft batch_size defaults and API validation for extremely large batches (issue #1187) owner: jamie, ETA: 2026-03-28. 6) billing credits proposal submitted to finance (done).
priya: we should also add a runbook step to proactively throttle on sustained p99 upstream latency > 1s for >2m. I'll update runbook.
alex: thanks everyone. final note: add link to incident traces in the ticket and schedule a 1hr postmortem session Monday 10:00 UTC. Closing triage for now but keep watchers if regressions appear. :thumbsup:
